summary: The bill repeals the U visa program for crime victims by striking section 101(a)(15)(U) of the Immigration and Nationality Act and making conforming amendments to remove all related provisions on eligibility, petitions, work authorization, and adjustment of status.

scores.thoughts: The bill text contains no provisions related to federal spending, appropriations, or budgetary matters. It solely repeals a visa category and makes conforming amendments to immigration law.

The bill directly repeals section 101(a)(15)(U) of the INA, eliminating the U visa program entirely along with associated benefits, waivers, and pathways to status. The findings explicitly criticize the program for enabling illegal immigration and fraud, and the legislation replaces it with narrower alternatives like the S visa or case-by-case parole. This constitutes a clear restriction on an existing immigration benefit.
